summary: FieldWitness is a no-login, offline-capable web application that helps farmers evaluate multi-season crop-rotation strategies without replacing local agronomic judgment. Across 200 pilot fields in the Kansas High Plains, USA (T14SLH) and 120 calibrated demo fields from 400 parcels in Central Ukraine (T36UVU), FieldWitness audits each field's Current rotation alongside three-season alternatives using three independent witnesses: (1) Physics — an FAO-56 root-zone water balance forced by NASA POWER daily meteorology and observed soil water capacities; (2) The Field's Own Past — Approximate Bayesian Computation calibrating soil/crop parameters against 30 m Harmonized Landsat Sentinel-2 and 20 m Sentinel-2 trajectories; and (3) Neighbours — causal Panel-OBDML/DAPSM natural experiments active in Ukraine and transparently turned OFF in Kansas where diagnostics failed. Every number carries an explicit provenance tag ([O], [D], [E], [A]) and an A–D evidence grade, paired with interactive maps, 3D soil twins, hazard calendars, and printable QR dossiers.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Project Overview & Impact:
FieldWitness is an open-source, offline-capable decision-support application designed to help farmers make more informed crop-rotation decisions using satellite observations, soil information, and agronomic science. It evaluates 320 calibrated fields across Kansas, USA (T14SLH), and Central Ukraine (T36UVU), providing transparent comparisons between current farming practices and alternative three-season rotations. The project reports a mean seasonal water-use reduction of 253.4 mm across Kansas pilot fields, alongside field-specific evidence and uncertainty indicators. Its goal is to make complex Earth observation data accessible and actionable without replacing local agricultural expertise.

Interactive Regional Maps & Synchronized NASA Trends:
FieldWitness visualizes current field conditions and Rank-1 versus Current rotation differences across 200 Kansas and 120 Central Ukraine fields. Interactive maps are synchronized with a multi-year Trend Scrubber displaying NASA GRACE/GRACE-FO, SMAP L4, and NASA POWER observations. A strict Pixel Scale Contract distinguishes field-level satellite evidence (20–30 m) from broader regional observations (9–55 km), preventing misleading comparisons across different spatial resolutions.

Three Independent Evidence Witnesses & Safety Circuit Breaker:
The decision-support engine combines three independent evidence sources. Witness 1 applies the FAO-56 daily root-zone water balance using NASA POWER meteorological data and soil-water-capacity estimates from USDA-NRCS SSURGO in Kansas (median TAW: 282.1 mm) and ISRIC SoilGrids 2.0 in Ukraine (median TAW: 206.5 mm), covering 0–135 cm soil depth [E]. Witness 2 analyzes 20–30 m Sentinel-2/HLS satellite histories using Time-Weighted Dynamic Time Warping (TWDTW), achieving 86.7% season matching, alongside Approximate Bayesian Computation (ABC) for soil and crop parameter calibration [D]. Witness 3 applies Panel-OBDML/DAPSM causal natural experiments, enabled in Ukraine after 30 pre-cutoff diagnostic checks passed, supporting Grade A evidence across 44 rotation options. It remains disabled in Kansas where diagnostic requirements were not met. This Safety Circuit Breaker prevents unreliable evidence from influencing recommendations.

Farmer-Controlled Rotation Decisions & 3D Field Twin:
Farmers can explore alternative crop rotations through deterministic Pareto ranking, adjusting six priority sliders and applying real farm constraints, including crop restrictions and irrigation availability. Interactive weather sensitivity scenarios test the effects of +1/+2 °C temperature changes and rainfall variations from -20% to +10%. The Field in 3D environment provides an interactive Three.js simulation of week-by-week root-zone water depletion using an in-browser FAO-56 solver, validated against its Python reference implementation with a numerical difference of only 5.7 × 10⁻⁶ mm.


Agricultural Risk Calendars, Global Evaluation & Shareable Reports:
A 12-month Bare-Soil Calendar identifies periods of soil exposure [O], highlighting potential agricultural vulnerabilities. It integrates Landsat 8/9 Land Surface Temperature observations (>35 °C) [O] and ERA5 extreme-rainfall indicators (>q99) [E]. The Add My Field feature allows users to evaluate additional farm coordinates globally using NASA POWER and SoilGrids 2.0 data directly within the application. Farmers can also generate printable one-page QR dossiers containing their selected priorities, rotation settings, and weather stress scenarios, making results easier to review and share.

Scientific Validity, Limitations & Technical Implementation


Scientific Honesty & Validation:
FieldWitness reports a non-monetary Relative Yield Index (0–1) rather than claiming actual crop yields or financial profits. It enforces a strict December 31, 2021 temporal leakage barrier to protect the integrity of historical evaluation and openly reports unsuccessful experiments and model limitations. Examples include disabling the Kansas Neighbours Witness when its causal diagnostics failed, reporting the 86.7% season-matching result against a 90% target, and documenting the improvement in Ukraine's maize-versus-sunflower separation from κ = 0.035 using NDVI alone to κ = 0.177 in 2021 with Sentinel-2 Red-Edge/SWIR features and the MAE-pretrained CropFormer model.

Technology Stack & Development Tools:
The application was developed using Python 3.12, TypeScript, React 19, and Vite. Its scientific and machine-learning components use NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn, DoubleML, Rasterio, GeoPandas, PyTorch, and Pydantic v2. Interactive geospatial visualization is powered by MapLibre GL JS and Three.js, while Cloudflare Workers provide an optional grounded-fact chat proxy. Automated testing and deployment use Vitest, Pytest, and GitHub Actions/Pages.

Innovation & Intended Impact:
The project's central innovation is its Evidence-Graded Decision Support architecture, combining agronomic physics, satellite-derived historical patterns, and causal machine learning instead of relying on a single prediction model. By allowing farmers to control decision priorities, inspect supporting evidence, explore climate scenarios, and identify uncertainty, FieldWitness aims to support more informed water management, reduce avoidable soil exposure, and encourage more sustainable crop-rotation planning.
